tagline: AI customer support platform: multi-tenant RAG chat widget with real-time human handoff

weeks.outcome: Monorepo runs locally, users can sign up as a business and log in with roles.
Docs (PDF / text / URL) are ingested in the background into pgvector.
First demo: a script-tag widget answers from the tenant's docs with sources.
Low-confidence chats escalate to a live agent inbox in real time.
Analytics (incl. unanswered questions) and Stripe billing with plan limits.
Tested, hardened, deployed live with README, diagram and demo video.

tasks.title: Repo setup (monorepo)
tasks.notes: Docker Compose for Postgres and Redis
tasks.goal: A pnpm + Turborepo monorepo where `docker compose up` plus `pnpm dev` runs every app locally.
subtasks: Init pnpm workspace + Turborepo: apps/api (NestJS), apps/worker, apps/dashboard (Next.js), apps/widget (Preact + Vite), packages/db, packages/shared, packages/config
Shared tsconfig, ESLint, Prettier, Husky + lint-staged, commitlint (Conventional Commits)
docker-compose.yml: pgvector/pgvector:pg16 + redis:7 with healthchecks and named volumes
packages/db: Drizzle ORM config and first migration that enables the `vector` extension
Typed env config validated with zod; .env.example for every app
GET /health endpoint that checks Postgres and Redis
Git init, push to GitHub, first CI run goes green
acceptance: Fresh clone: `docker compose up -d && pnpm i && pnpm dev` starts api, dashboard and widget dev server
GET /health returns {db: ok, redis: ok}
`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` pass locally and in CI
tasks.talking_point: Turborepo caches per package, so CI only rebuilds what actually changed.

tasks.title: Auth with roles
tasks.goal: Secure dashboard login with role-based access; every request carries a verified tenant context.
subtasks: tenants + users tables and migrations; argon2 password hashing
POST /auth/login, /auth/refresh, /auth/logout: 15-min access JWT + rotating refresh token in httpOnly cookie
JWT claims: sub, tenantId, role; TenantContext populated by a global guard
@Roles() decorator + RolesGuard (owner > admin > agent)
Invite flow: owner/admin invites agents by email (invite token; email printed to console in dev)
Dashboard: login page, auth middleware, role-aware navigation
Unit tests for guards; integration tests for login / refresh / logout
acceptance: An agent calling an admin-only endpoint gets 403 (covered by a test)
Refresh token rotation works and logout invalidates the refresh token
Password hashes are never logged or returned by any endpoint
tasks.talking_point: The tenant id comes from the verified token, never from the request body, so users cannot spoof another tenant.

tasks.title: Tenant onboarding
tasks.goal: A business signs up and gets a tenant, an owner account and a widget public key in under a minute.
subtasks: POST /auth/signup creates tenant + owner in one DB transaction
Public key generation (pk_live_ + random) and key rotation endpoint
Branding settings (jsonb): primary color, logo, greeting, launcher position
Allowed domains list per tenant (used by the widget origin check)
Onboarding wizard: company name -> branding -> copy embed snippet
Public GET /widget/config?key=pk_... returns branding only, never secrets
Seed script: demo tenant 'Acme Bikes' with sample docs for the live demo
acceptance: Signup lands on a dashboard showing the embed snippet with that tenant's key
Rotating the key invalidates the old key immediately
Widget config endpoint exposes only public fields (test)
tasks.talking_point: The public key identifies the tenant; the allowed-domains check stops someone else embedding a client's widget.

tasks.title: Knowledge base upload
tasks.goal: Admins add knowledge from PDF, plain text / markdown, or a public URL.
subtasks: documents table: title, source_type (pdf/text/url), source, status (queued/processing/ready/failed), error, chunk_count
POST /documents (multipart, 10 MB limit, MIME + magic-byte check) and POST /documents/url
StorageService: local disk in dev, S3-compatible (e.g. Cloudflare R2) in prod
URL fetching with SSRF protection: http(s) only, block private / loopback / metadata IPs, size + timeout limits
Dashboard Knowledge Base page: drag-and-drop upload, status badges, delete, re-index
Enqueue an ingestion job on create (consumed by T06)
acceptance: PDF, TXT, MD and URL can be added from the UI and appear with status `queued`
Oversized or unsupported files are rejected with clear error messages
URLs resolving to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 are rejected (test)
tasks.talking_point: URL ingestion is an SSRF risk, so the fetcher resolves DNS and blocks private IP ranges before connecting.

tasks.title: Chunking and embeddings
tasks.goal: Turn documents into searchable vector chunks, always scoped to one tenant.
subtasks: Text extraction: PDF parser, HTML readability for URLs, raw text / markdown
Chunker: split on headings / paragraphs, ~500-800 tokens, 10-15% overlap, keep title + heading path as metadata
EmbeddingProvider interface (provider + model from env), batched calls with retry and backoff
document_chunks table with vector column, HNSW index (vector_cosine_ops) and tenant_id index
searchChunks(tenantId, embedding, k) repository function: tenant filter is mandatory
Tests: chunk boundaries and overlap; similarity search returns the expected chunk
acceptance: A 20-page PDF becomes embedded chunks in Postgres
Searching a known phrase returns the right chunk in the top 3
Search never returns another tenant's chunk (test)
tasks.talking_point: One Postgres holds relational data and vectors, so tenant filtering and joins happen in the same query as similarity search.

tasks.title: Background ingestion job
tasks.goal: Ingestion runs off the request path and is retryable and observable.
subtasks: BullMQ `ingestion` queue on Redis, consumed by apps/worker
Job pipeline: extract -> chunk -> embed -> upsert, updating documents.status at each step
3 retries with exponential backoff; failed jobs keep the error message
Idempotent re-index: replace old chunks in the same transaction
Live status updates in the dashboard (Redis pub/sub -> socket, polling as fallback)
Worker concurrency limit and graceful shutdown; Bull Board UI in dev
acceptance: Upload request returns immediately; the worker processes in the background
Killing the worker mid-job: the job retries and completes after restart
A failed document shows the reason in the UI and can be retried
tasks.talking_point: Embedding is slow and rate-limited, so it runs in a queue with retries instead of blocking the upload request.

tasks.title: RAG chat API
tasks.goal: Answer customer questions using only the tenant's docs, streamed token by token, with sources and a confidence score.
subtasks: conversations + messages tables (status ai/waiting/human/closed; sources jsonb; confidence)
Pipeline: PII redaction -> embed question -> top-k chunks for the tenant -> prompt -> streamed LLM answer
Prompt rules: answer only from context, otherwise say so; context wrapped as untrusted data; last N messages as memory
Structured metadata per answer: confidence (0-1), cited chunk ids, needs_human flag
Confidence = blend of retrieval similarity and model self-rating (formula documented in ARCHITECTURE.md)
LlmProvider interface; provider and model chosen via env
POST /v1/chat with Server-Sent Events, sharing the same ChatService the socket gateway uses
Persist every message with sources + confidence; write usage_events
acceptance: A question covered by the docs gets a streamed answer with at least one correct citation
A question not covered gets an honest 'I don't know' with low confidence
First token arrives in under 2 seconds locally
tasks.talking_point: The model can only answer from retrieved chunks and must cite them, which keeps answers grounded and auditable.

tasks.title: Embeddable widget
tasks.goal: Any website adds one script tag and gets a branded chat bubble.
subtasks: Preact + Vite library build to a single IIFE widget.js, target < 50 KB gzipped
Render inside Shadow DOM so host-page CSS and widget CSS never clash
Read data-key from the script tag, fetch /widget/config, apply branding
Socket.io client on the /widget namespace, authenticated with public key + anonymous visitor id
UI: launcher, chat panel, streaming text, source links, 'Talk to a human' button, reconnect state
Origin check against the tenant's allowed domains on connect
Demo host page and install snippet shown in the dashboard
acceptance: Pasting the snippet into a plain HTML file shows a working, branded widget
Host-page CSS does not affect the widget and vice versa
CI fails if the bundle grows beyond 60 KB gzipped
tasks.talking_point: Shadow DOM plus a tiny Preact bundle means the widget drops into any client site without breaking their styles.

tasks.title: Agent inbox
tasks.goal: Agents see live conversations and can jump in from the dashboard.
subtasks: Socket.io /agent namespace with JWT auth and the Redis adapter for multiple API instances
Rooms: tenant:{id} and conversation:{id}
Inbox tabs: Needs agent / Mine / AI-handled / Closed with live unread counts
Conversation view: full history with AI sources and confidence visible to agents
Agent reply box: message saved as sender_type=agent and pushed to the widget instantly
Claim / assign conversation (assigned_agent_id), exclusive claim
acceptance: A new widget conversation appears in the inbox without a refresh
Two agents in two browsers see the same state; claiming is exclusive
Works with 2 API instances running (Redis adapter)
tasks.talking_point: The Redis adapter fans socket events out across API instances, so the app scales horizontally.

tasks.title: Handoff logic
tasks.goal: Low-confidence or explicit requests move the chat to a human, and back to AI when done.
subtasks: Conversation state machine: ai -> waiting -> human -> ai | closed, all transitions in one service
Triggers: confidence below tenant threshold (default 0.55), 'Talk to a human' button, intent phrases, 2 low-confidence answers in a row
Waiting state: customer sees 'Connecting you to an agent', inbox highlights and notifies
While status = human the AI pipeline is skipped for that conversation
Agent actions: hand back to AI, close conversation
No agent online: collect the customer's email and save it as an offline ticket
Tenant setting: confidence threshold slider
Unit tests for every valid and invalid transition
acceptance: A low-confidence question shows under 'Needs agent' within 1 second
The AI never replies while status = human (test)
Handing back to AI resumes AI answers
tasks.talking_point: Handoff is an explicit state machine, so every transition is validated and testable instead of scattered if-statements.

tasks.title: Typing, presence, history
tasks.goal: The chat feels live: typing indicators, agent presence, and history that survives reloads.
subtasks: Typed socket event contract in packages/shared (zod) used by api, dashboard and widget
Throttled typing:start / typing:stop in both directions
Agent presence (online / away / offline) in Redis with TTL heartbeats; widget shows 'agents online'
Paginated message history on widget reopen and in the agent view
Read receipts and unread counts
Reconnect + missed-message sync (fetch since lastMessageId)
acceptance: Typing shows on the other side within ~300 ms
Closing and reopening the widget restores the conversation
Agent presence flips to offline when the tab closes (TTL expiry)
tasks.talking_point: Presence uses Redis keys with TTL heartbeats, so crashed clients go offline automatically.

tasks.title: Analytics dashboard
tasks.notes: AI vs. human resolution, top questions, unanswered questions
tasks.goal: Show the client the value of the AI and exactly which docs are missing.
subtasks: KPIs: conversations, AI-resolved %, handoff %, avg first response time, thumbs up/down rating
Top questions: group similar questions by embedding similarity
Unanswered questions report: low-confidence / handed-off questions grouped, with an 'Add doc' shortcut
Date range filter, charts (Recharts), Redis cache for 5 minutes
CSV export
acceptance: Seeded demo data shows meaningful charts
Unanswered report lists questions the AI failed on, with counts
Every analytics query is tenant-scoped (test)
tasks.talking_point: The unanswered-questions report turns AI failures into a to-do list of docs the client should write.

tasks.title: Stripe billing and plan limits
tasks.goal: Real SaaS billing: plans, upgrades and limits enforced from usage.
subtasks: Plans in config: Free (100 AI msgs/mo, 5 docs, 1 agent), Pro, Business
Stripe Checkout for upgrades and Customer Portal for manage / cancel
Webhook endpoint with signature verification, idempotent by event id
Handle checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.updated / deleted, invoice.payment_failed
subscriptions table synced from webhooks (Stripe is the source of truth)
PlanLimitGuard reads monthly usage_events; at the limit the widget falls back to 'leave a message'
Billing page: current plan, usage meters, upgrade CTA
acceptance: Test-mode upgrade works end to end (Stripe CLI webhook forwarding)
Exceeding the Free limit blocks AI answers gracefully
A replayed webhook does not double-apply
tasks.talking_point: Webhooks are verified and idempotent, and plan state is derived from Stripe, never trusted from the client.

tasks.title: Tests
tasks.goal: Prove it works: automated tests on every PR plus a measurable answer-quality score.
subtasks: Unit: chunker, confidence scorer, handoff state machine, guards, PII redactor (written alongside each task, consolidated here)
Integration: API against real Postgres/pgvector + Redis (CI service containers)
Tenant isolation suite: tenant A can never read tenant B's docs, chunks or conversations through any endpoint
E2E (Playwright): signup -> upload doc -> ask in widget -> handoff -> agent reply
Eval set: 30-40 questions for the demo tenant (answerable, unanswerable, injection attempts)
Eval scorer: retrieval hit@k, answer correctness, correct-refusal rate; writes a report
Coverage report; target >= 70% on core services
acceptance: CI runs unit + integration tests on every PR
Eval workflow publishes a score report; the baseline is recorded in docs
Isolation suite passes
tasks.talking_point: The eval set turns 'the AI seems good' into a number that CI tracks across prompt and model changes.

tasks.title: Security hardening
tasks.notes: Rate limiting, prompt-injection and PII safeguards
tasks.goal: Close the gaps most portfolio projects leave open.
subtasks: Rate limiting per IP and per tenant (Redis store) on auth, widget and chat; socket message rate limit
Prompt-injection defense: user input and retrieved docs treated as untrusted data, system prompt never echoed, pattern checks, output filter
PII redaction (emails, phones, card numbers with Luhn check) before LLM calls and in logs
Postgres Row-Level Security on tenant tables as defense in depth (app.tenant_id set per transaction)
Helmet, strict CORS, input validation everywhere, dependency audit
docs/SECURITY.md: one-page threat model
acceptance: A burst of 100 requests/second from one IP receives 429s
Injection prompts from the eval set do not change behavior
PII is masked in stored logs and in the LLM payload (test)
RLS blocks a cross-tenant query even with the app filter removed (test)
tasks.talking_point: Tenant isolation has three layers: token-derived context, scoped repositories, and Postgres RLS as a safety net.

tasks.title: CI/CD and deployment
tasks.goal: Merge to main and it is live, with no manual steps.
subtasks: Multi-stage Dockerfiles for api and worker (node:22-alpine, non-root, small images)
Finish ci.yml: docker build check and widget bundle-size check
Dashboard + widget CDN on Vercel; api, worker, Postgres (pgvector) and Redis on Railway (Render as fallback)
deploy.yml: migrate DB -> deploy api/worker -> deploy dashboard -> smoke test /health
GitHub Environments with secrets; Vercel preview deploys for PRs
Production demo tenant seeded + public demo page
Uptime monitor and error tracking (Sentry free tier)
acceptance: Merge to main goes live in under 10 minutes without manual steps
Public demo URL works on desktop and mobile
Rollback steps documented in PIPELINE.md
tasks.talking_point: Every PR runs lint, types, tests against real Postgres + Redis, and a bundle-size budget before it can merge.

tasks.title: README, architecture diagram, demo video
tasks.goal: A recruiter understands the project in 60 seconds; a client sees something they would pay for.
subtasks: README: hero GIF, live demo + demo login, features, diagram, stack, multi-tenancy explainer, 3-command setup, test + eval results
Architecture diagram exported as PNG/SVG (Mermaid source kept in docs)
2-3 min demo video: signup -> upload -> widget answer with sources -> handoff -> agent reply -> analytics -> billing
Portfolio case study / LinkedIn post
Client-facing one-pager (white-label pitch) and final pass on the Word project document
acceptance: Someone new can run the project locally by following only the README
README, demo video and live URL are linked from resume / portfolio
tasks.talking_point: Walk through the demo video live: it shows the whole product loop in under three minutes.
